data.summary: The pinsregen git merge driver (ddflow pins regenerate --install) keeps our side of the WHOLE pin file on any merge. For a mixed file such as README.md (prose plus generated tables, and [pins] lists it) that drops the other side's non-conflicting prose edits silently; the post-merge hook regenerates only the generated blocks, so the loss is not noticed. services/pins_merge.py merge_driver returns 0 leaving ours untouched. The merge queue's integrator now resolves only the conflicting hunks (git merge-file --ours); the driver should do the same: run git merge-file --ours %A %O %B with the three versions it is given.
data.title: pinsregen merge driver drops the other side's prose edits in a mixed pin file (README.md)

chunk_findings.detail: The docstring says `timeout_s` replaces `[ci].timeout_s` "when it is positive", but the implementation uses `timeout_s or cfg.ci.timeout_s`, which only treats 0 as "unset". Given `timeout_s=-1` (e.g. a caller passing a negative `--timeout N` before the config-side `int_at_least(0)` validation, which only covers the config file value, not the function argument), the call passes `timeout_s=-1` to the subprocess runner instead of falling back to `cfg.ci.timeout_s`, so the CI run would fail or time out immediately rather than using the configured timeout.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:run

chunk_findings.detail: `holder()` takes the integrator lock itself (`fsio.file_lock(_dir(repo) / "integrator.lock", 0)`) to test whether anyone holds it. Because the integrator also acquires that lock with a zero timeout (`integrator()` calls `fsio.file_lock(d / "integrator.lock", 0)` and yields False on `LockTimeout`), a status check that lands in the gap between an integrator's process start and its lock acquisition — or simply concurrent with it — makes the real integrator see the lock as held and yield False, refusing to run even though no other integrator exists. Interleaving: process A calls `holder()` and acquires the lock; process B calls `integrator()` at that instant, gets `LockTimeout`, and reports "another integrator holds it", so the queue head is never landed in that run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergequeue.py holder

chunk_findings.detail: `took[-window:]` with `window=0` evaluates to `took[-0:]`, which is the entire list, not the empty slice: `typical_s(rows, window=0, default_s=60)` returns the mean over all merged entries instead of falling back to `default_s`. Since the conformance requirement makes every number a knob, a project that sets the ETA window to 0 (meaning "ignore history, use the default") silently gets a full-history average instead.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergequeue.py typical_s

chunk_findings.detail: The added test block re-imports, mid-file with `noqa: E402`, every name it relies on (`os`, `subprocess`, `sys`, `time`, `Path`, `pytest`, `append_config`, `pass_pipeline`, `MQ`) — yet it uses `json` extensively (`json.loads(out)["worktree"]` in `_finish`, `json.loads(out)["entries"]` in `_status`, `json.loads(out)` in `_ci_outcome`, `json.loads(out)["processed"]` and `json.loads(out)` in the integrator tests) without importing it in the block. The deliberate pattern of re-importing even certainly-already-imported names like `Path` and `pytest` indicates the author treated this block as self-contained and simply forgot `import json`; if the file header at line 1 does not already import `json` (nothing in the pre-existing 162 lines shown uses it — the visible earlier test only does string matching on `out`), the first call to `_finish` raises `NameError: name 'json' is not defined` and every new test in this block fails at collection-run time. Given the exhaustive re-import list, this is very likely a genuine omission rather than reliance on the header.

chunk_findings.detail: `remove()` promises to drop an entry "any state but running", but it is not synchronised with the integrator: it reads the entry with `get()` and then unlinks the file, with no lock and no re-check. Given an integrator that calls `take(repo, e)` (setting the entry to RUNNING and rewriting the file) in the gap between `remove`'s `get()` (which saw the entry as QUEUED) and its `_path(...).unlink()`, the unlink succeeds and the caller is told the item was removed — yet the integrator is already landing that item and `finish()` will rewrite the entry as MERGED. So a user who removes a queued item to stop it being merged can observe a successful removal while the item is merged anyway. The state check needs to happen under a lock shared with `take` (or the integrator must re-verify the entry still exists before merging).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/mergequeue.py remove

chunk_findings.detail: The test fabricates a stale `integrator.json` using the pid of a process it has just reaped (`gone = Popen(...); gone.wait()`). A reaped pid is immediately eligible for reuse by the OS, and this very test then spawns several new processes (`run_cli` invocations for `_finish`, `_queue`, and `queue run`). If any of those subprocesses (or a grandchild) is assigned `gone.pid`, `MQ.holder(proj)` — which liveness-checks the pid — will see a live process and report a holder, making the first assertion fail or, worse, making `queue run` refuse with "another integrator" so the test fails spuriously. On a busy CI machine with rapid pid turnover this is a real flake source; the test should instead use a pid guaranteed dead (e.g. scan upward from `os.getpid()` for a pid that fails `os.kill(pid, 0)`) rather than a recently-freed one.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_merge_queue.py:test_a_crashed_integrators_leftover_is_no_holder_and_does_not_block_the_line

data.body: DX-merge-queue shipped ddflow queue add|run|status|remove. The item also named ddflow merge --queue; the merge Command lives in surfaces/declared/lifecycle.py, which fleet-gatedx held (fix-Bc262739f62) for the whole run, so the flag was left out. Add Param queue (boolean) to the merge Command, call api.queue_add(repo, id, agent=agent) when set (not merge_item), and make MERGE_PAYLOAD/merge_body/merge_notes/merge_text/merge_reason in lifecycle_cli.py handle the queued result (data keys id, queued, added, state, position, eta_s, text; its dirty refusal must not advise --allow-dirty). Mind the tools/list byte budget (tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py): merge gains an argument; trim its other helps. Regression test: tests/test_merge_queue.py enqueues with merge --queue (CLI and MCP bodies equal).
